passages.provision_quote: An employer shall not rely solely on an ADS when making a discipline, termination, or deactivation decision.
passages.note: Authored bill mandating pre-use notice, use prohibitions and human review of automated decision systems by employers, but it requires no safety testing and imposes no liability on developers.

rows.reasoning: McNerney authored SB 7 (2025-2026), which requires employers to give written notice of automated decision systems and provides that "An employer shall not rely solely on an ADS when making a discipline, termination, or deactivation decision." That places him well past "Allow AI companies to develop and deploy technology freely without government interference" and "Suggest AI safety guidelines but let companies choose whether to follow them", but it does not "Require safety testing before AI can be used in high-stakes areas like hiring, healthcare, and policing" (the bill's pre-use obligation is notice, not testing), and its enforcement runs against employers who deploy an ADS rather than to "Hold AI developers legally responsible when their systems cause harm". The bill establishes a side without matching the clauses of any single rung.
